mainTopic: A נדר against meat or wine: are gravy, sediments, and cooked dishes that carry their flavor also forbidden?
overview: This amud finishes a משנה about someone who vowed off meat. The תנא קמא says he may still eat the gravy and the sediments, but רבי יהודה forbids them. רבי יהודה backs himself up with a story where רבי טרפון forbade even eggs that were cooked with the meat. The חכמים agree the story happened, but they say it was about a vow on one specific piece of meat ('this meat'). When a specific forbidden item gets mixed into other food and its taste can be felt (נותן טעם), the mixture is forbidden. A general vow on 'meat' covers only the meat itself. The משנה then applies the same rule to wine. A general vow against wine allows a dish that tastes of wine, but a vow on 'this wine' forbids a dish it fell into if its taste comes through.

steps.title: Vowing off meat: gravy and sediments are permitted, but רבי יהודה forbids
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא rules that one who vowed off meat may eat the gravy and sediments. רבי יהודה disagrees and forbids them.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One who vows off meat] is permitted to eat the gravy and the sediments. But רבי יהודה forbids them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its ruling about a person who vowed not to eat meat. It says the gravy and sediments are still allowed, and then records that רבי יהודה disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion holds that a vow on 'meat' covers only actual meat, not the liquid or leftover bits from cooking it. רבי יהודה holds that these by-products are included in the vow. The rest of the section examines this disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: Gravy, the liquid the meat was cooked in
Sediments or small bits that settle at the bottom of the pot

phrases.english: is permitted in the gravy and the sediments,
phrases.notes: The beginning of this case, 'one who vows off meat,' is on the previous page.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּתָּר בָּרוֹטֶב וּבַקֵּיפֶה, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹסֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה's case of one who vows off meat, which began on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, a vow against meat does not forbid gravy or sediments. רבי יהודה forbids them.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's proof: רבי טרפון forbade even eggs cooked with the meat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה tells a story in which רבי טרפון forbade eggs that were cooked together with the meat. This supports his stricter view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: There was a case where רבי טרפון forbade us even eggs that were cooked with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה brings a real story to back up his opinion. רבי טרפון forbade the eggs that had been cooked together with meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even eggs, which are not meat at all, were forbidden just because they were cooked with meat, then surely gravy and sediments are forbidden too. This is רבי יהודה's argument from a מעשה (an actual ruling).

keyTerms.meaning: An actual incident or ruling, used as proof

phrases.english: There was an incident, and Rabbi Tarfon forbade to us
eggs that were cooked with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה וְאָסַר עָלֵינוּ רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יהודה's stricter opinion from step 1.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that a vow against meat also forbids things cooked with it
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ruling by רבי טרפון forbidding eggs cooked with the meat

steps.title: The חכמים: that story was about a vow on 'this meat'
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים agree with the story but limit it. It applies only when someone vowed on a specific piece of meat, because a specific forbidden item that mixes into other food forbids that food if its taste is felt.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: That is true, but when? When he says 'This meat is forbidden to me.' This is because when someone vows off a specific item and it gets mixed into another food, if it gives flavor, the mixture is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה's proof. They accept that רבי טרפון ruled this way, but they say the case was a vow on one specific piece of meat, not on meat in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is turned aside, not denied. When a person forbids a particular item ('this meat'), that item acts like a forbidden food, so whatever it mixes into is forbidden if its taste is felt (נותן טעם). A general vow on 'meat' covers only meat itself, so gravy and sediments stay permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: It is indeed so (agreeing, then limiting)
'This meat', a vow on one specific item
Gives flavor, meaning its taste can be felt in the mixture

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying רבי טרפון was wrong. They agree with his ruling but say it only applies to a vow on a specific piece of meat ('this meat'), not to a general vow against meat.
steps.whatToRemember: A general vow ('meat') forbids only the thing itself. A vow on a specific item ('this meat') makes it forbid any mixture where its taste is felt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key difference between vowing off a general type of food and vowing off a specific item. The משנה uses the same difference again for wine.

phrases.english: They said to him: So it is,
phrases.notes: 'They' are the חכמים, the first opinion in the משנה.

phrases.english: but when? At a time that he says:

phrases.notes: He means 'this particular meat is forbidden to me.'

phrases.english: because one who vows off an item
and it became mixed with another,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: if there is enough of it to give flavor, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns aside רבי יהודה's proof by limiting the story to a vow on a specific item.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Accepts the story but rejects using it as proof for a general vow against meat
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי טרפון's case was a vow on a specific piece of meat ('this meat'), where the rule of נותן טעם applies. A general vow on meat is different.

steps.title: The same rule for wine: a general vow versus 'this wine'
steps.stepSummary: One who vows off wine may eat a dish that tastes of wine. But if he vowed off 'this wine' and it fell into a dish, the dish is forbidden if the wine's taste is felt.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who vows off wine is permitted to eat a cooked dish that has the taste of wine. If he said 'This wine is קונם, so I will not taste it,' and it fell into a cooked dish, if it gives flavor, the dish is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same difference to wine. A general vow allows a dish that tastes of wine, but a vow on specific wine forbids a dish it fell into, if the taste comes through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the meat case exactly. 'Wine' in general does not include a cooked dish with a wine flavor. Specific wine that was made forbidden ('this wine') forbids a mixture where its taste is felt (נותן טעם).

keyTerms.meaning: A word used to make a vow, like saying 'forbidden as a קרבן'

steps.whatToRemember: Meat and wine follow the same rule. A general vow forbids only the item itself, while a vow on a specific item forbids any mixture where its taste is felt.

phrases.aramaic: מוּתָּר בְּתַבְשִׁיל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ טַעַם יַיִן.
phrases.english: is permitted in a cooked dish that has the taste of wine.
If he said: "This wine is konam, that I taste it,"
phrases.notes: He means 'this wine is forbidden to me, so I will not taste it.'

phrases.english: and it fell into a cooked dish,
if there is enough of it to give flavor,

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הַיַּיִן — מוּתָּר בְּתַבְשִׁיל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ טַעַם יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the general-versus-specific rule from step 3 to wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A general vow against wine allows a dish with a wine flavor. A vow on 'this wine' forbids a dish it fell into if the wine's taste is felt.
